key_insight: This paper shows how to perform discrete-token diffusion directly on high-dimensional pretrained visual representations, preserving rich semantics while enabling a unified token-prediction generation paradigm similar to language models.
problem_solved: Existing discrete visual-generation methods restrict tokens to low-dimensional latents (8–32 dims), losing semantic richness; generating discrete high-dimensional representations (768–1024 dims) is combinatorially hard and unstable with prior discrete diffusion techniques.
method: Introduce a 'cubic' factorization of high-dimensional representation tokens that breaks each vector into structured subcomponents amenable to discrete modeling.
Design a discrete diffusion process and noise schedule that operate on the factorized components, together with a denoising network that predicts component tokens in a categorical/tokenwise manner.

Leverage pretrained high-dimensional encoders as targets/conditioning and train the diffusion denoiser to reconstruct their discrete factor components, enabling efficient sampling and scalable token prediction.
impact: Enables language-model-style discrete generation for richer visual representations, improving semantic fidelity and simplifying integration into multimodal architectures; useful for practitioners building generative vision–language systems and token-based pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: pretrained encoder → cubic factorization → discrete diffusion denoiser → reconstructed tokens
Illustration of cubic factorization: high-dim vector split into a 3D/block grid of sub-tokens
Comparison chart: low-dimensional discrete tokens vs cubic high-dimensional tokens (semantic fidelity, token count, generation quality)
Sampling trajectory visualization: noisy-to-clean token transitions across diffusion steps
paper_title: Cubic Discrete Diffusion: Discrete Visual Generation on High-Dimensional Representation Tokens
paper_authors: Yuqing Wang, Chuofan Ma, Zhijie Lin, Yao Teng, Lijun Yu
